title: Decide the counterexample tag: column, widened shape, or documented floor
description: The resolution side of the tag decision closed on 2026-10-07 as the resolves_named column; the counterexample side is open. Measured 2026-10-06: 74 of 372 families use counterexample language in title or abstract and only 44 carry the counterexample tag; of the 31 untagged flags, 30 are genuine in kind and the false positive is 348, matched through 'nonnegatively'. Three options: (a) add a counterex_named column and keep the shape at 44; (b) widen the shape to 74; (c) leave 44 as a documented floor with no code change. title: Render the index pages from the ledger joins
description:
Write notes/scripts/build_index.py, stdlib only, no Lean: emit the entry point plus one page per family and per discipline. Each family page carries: number, title, discipline, claim shapes, tier, then links to every manuscript (PDF, its build/source LaTeX tree, its README.md), the Lean module directory and the main_results declaration for each formalized manuscript, lean/docs/<NNN>.md when a scope note exists, the comparator challenge configs, the reasoning trace when published, and the verification/ tree when shipped.

Reuse the joins in build_catalog.py rather than re-deriving them: formalized manuscripts come from the sources: id: ../preprints/... paths, and Lean file paths come from status.main_results entries reached through the family's comparator config stems. The family->Lean link is a name-based join through the config stem, so a family with challenges but no main_results entry has no Lean file to link — render that as absent, not as zero.

Acceptance: byte-identical on rerun; every family in notes/catalog.tsv has a page; the page count and the link counts reconcile with a fresh generator report (372 families, 722 manuscripts, 162 formalized, 235 scope notes, 405 challenges, 10 traces, 30 verification dirs).

title: Build the topic vocabulary and assign families to topics
description:
The request is "find all the manifold-related proofs", and nothing in the repo answers that today: the 17 disciplines in overview.tex are the release's coarse grouping, and the 23 Lean discipline directories (Analysis, NumberTheory, Combinatorics, Geometry, Probability, ...) are a second, finer grouping that does not align with the 17.

Build notes/topics.tsv as a curated vocabulary the generator validates against, then assign each family to zero or more topics by matching the vocabulary against title, abstract, scope note text, and Lean module path. Emit index/topics/<term>.md listing the families, and print the unassigned-term report so the vocabulary grows from evidence rather than from guesses.

Follow the conditional-tag discipline: a topic term is quotable only after it discriminates. The conditional regex flagged 9 families and 5 were not assumptions, so report per-term yield and quote the false positives. Topics are a column and a page, never a replacement for shapes.

title: Fix the index schema: node and edge tables, store format, location
description:
Decide before rendering anything. The node set is fixed by the release: 372 families, 722 manuscripts, 23 Lean discipline dirs, 554 Lean module dirs, 405 comparator challenges, 178 unique main_results configs, 235 scope notes, 10 traces, 30 verification dirs. The edge set: family->manuscript (722), family->discipline (372), manuscript->Lean file (162 formalized), family->challenge (405), config->declaration (185), manuscript->cited work (12,928 bib entries), plus the derived topic and name edges.

Open forks to settle, in order:
1. Store. Generated markdown plus TSV edge lists in git (reviewable, greppable, byte-identical regeneration, stdlib only) is the recommendation. A graph database is not: ~2,700 nodes and ~17,000 edges is a dict lookup, and Neo4j/Kuzu/Memgraph add a server, a binary store that cannot be reviewed in a diff, and a dependency the generator rules exclude. SQLite (stdlib sqlite3) is the middle option and belongs in a later child, built on demand from the TSV, not tracked.
2. Location. Root index/ is discoverable from README.md; notes/index/ keeps it beside the ledger. Pick one.
3. Granularity. Per-family pages (372) is the floor; per-manuscript pages (722) only if the manuscript page carries something the family page cannot.
4. Topic vocabulary. Curated file the generator validates against, versus auto-derived terms, versus the Lean module path hierarchy alone.

Record the decision in notes/index-design.md with the measured sizes that justify it.

title: Build a navigable index directory over families, manuscripts, and Lean source
description:
The release's own navigation is README.md plus CONTENTS.md, and CONTENTS.md is 9,169 lines of HTML tables linking PDFs only — no link from a family to its LaTeX source, its Lean module, its scope note, its comparator challenges, or its verification bundle. Answering "where is the Lean source for family 087" means four files and a name-based guess.

All the joins already exist in build_catalog.py: family -> manuscript paths (overview.tex/CONTENTS.md), manuscript -> formalized flag (formalization.yaml sources: id: ../preprints/...), family -> comparator configs -> main_results entries, and main_results carries both the declaration and the Lean file path (OAI/<Discipline>/<Module>/Main.lean). The index is a rendering of joins the ledger already computes, not new analysis.

Measured 2026-10-07 for sizing: 372 families, 722 manuscripts, 23 Lean discipline directories, 554 Lean module directories, 121,734 .lean files, 405 challenges, 178 unique main_results configs, 235 scope notes, 10 traces, 30 verification dirs, 12,928 bib entries across 501 .bib files.

Static reading only: never run lake, lean, or comparator. Every count quoted in a child comes from a fresh build_catalog.py report.

title: Roll the notes/ reading records into one findings index
description:
Reading findings are scattered by method, not by family: notes/t0-triage.md (137 families), notes/resolution-tag.md (233), notes/conditional.md (9 flagged, 5 real), notes/verification-dirs.md (30 dirs). Answering "what did we conclude about family NNN" means reading four documents and matching by hand.

Build notes/findings.tsv, one row per family: fam, discipline, claim shape, tier, evidence columns from the ledger, the reading verdict where one exists, and which notes/ document the verdict comes from. Generated by a stdlib script over notes/*.md plus notes/catalog.tsv, byte-identical on rerun, reconciling 372 rows. Findings stay in the tracked notes/ files; the index is a join, not a new record of record.

title: Index the 722 manuscript sources into notes/sources.tsv
description:
Write notes/scripts/build_sources.py, stdlib only, no Lean, no PDF parsing: for each of the 722 preprints/<dir>/, emit family dir, manuscript PDF path, main tex path, tex file count, .bib count, section count, \begin{proof} count, theorem-like environment count, abstract present, total tex bytes.

Main-file resolution rule, measured 2026-10-07: 717 of 722 directories contain exactly one file with \documentclass and 5 contain two or three; the documentclass file is main.tex in 495, paper.tex in 210, and one of 21 other names in the remaining 17 (preamble.tex 8, manuscript.tex 3, common.tex 2, and 4 singletons). Prefer main.tex/paper.tex, fall back to the \documentclass file, and flag multi-root directories rather than guessing.

Acceptance: 722 rows; running the script twice yields byte-identical output; the family set and manuscript PDF paths reconcile with notes/catalog.tsv with zero differences.

title: Mine the manuscript LaTeX sources under preprints/
description:
preprints/ is not PDF-only. Measured 2026-10-07: all 722 family directories ship the manuscript as LaTeX source — 7,729 .tex files, 501 .bib, 128 MB of source, 177 KB average per family. Every directory has exactly one PDF at its root (the manuscript, named article.pdf in most, paper.pdf/main.pdf/manuscript.pdf/final.pdf in the rest) plus a build/ tree holding the source and a README.md citation stub.

Content signals already present in the sources, counted corpus-wide: 20,449 \begin{proof}, 21,317 theorem/lemma/proposition/corollary/claim/conjecture environments, and \begin{abstract} in 722 of 722 directories. The ledger uses none of this: its abstracts come from overview.tex, and its claim shapes are derived from those abstracts alone.

Children add a source index, cross-check the two abstracts, test proof density as a ledger signal, build the citation graph, and inventory numbered results. All of it is static reading over text files: never run lake, lean, or comparator, and quote counts only from a fresh build_catalog.py report.

title: Build the name index from titles, theorem names, and bib authors
description:
"Cauchy-related" is a name query, and names sit in four places: family and manuscript titles, the 21,317 theorem-like environments in the LaTeX sources, the declaration names in status.main_results (OAI.CauchyDiagonal.main), and the author fields of the 12,928 bib entries.

Extract candidate names from those four sources, normalize the spelling variants the sources disagree on (Mézard–Parisi vs Mezard-Parisi, Kaplansky's vs Kaplansky), and emit index/names/<name>.md listing families, manuscripts, and Lean declarations. State per source which names came from body text versus titles, because a name appearing in a body paragraph is a citation, not a subject.

Acceptance: every name page resolves to at least one family; the union of name pages covers the 10 published reasoning-trace families by construction; report the count of name pages and the families with no name hit.

title: Check index link integrity against the shipped files
description:
Every link the index emits must resolve on disk. Check all of them: manuscript PDFs (722, named article.pdf/paper.pdf/main.pdf/manuscript.pdf/final.pdf/full-title), LaTeX source trees under build/, README.md stubs (722), Lean module directories, scope notes (235), challenge configs (405), traces (10 files for 10 traces — the Mezard-Parisi trace ships as both .pdf and .tex), verification dirs (30).

Report broken links as a count with the list, and reconcile the totals against a fresh build_catalog.py report. A link that resolves to a directory is not a link to a file: state which.
notes: Measured 2026-10-07: CONTENTS.md already links all 722 manuscript PDFs and all 235 scope notes with zero broken links — verified with the paren-safe path regex preprints/(?:[^\s(){}\]|\([0-9]+\))*\.pdf. A naive [^)]* regex reports 721 and invents a missing link, because one path contains parentheses: preprints/Sharp-integral-fillings-in-CAT(0)-spaces-September-23-2026/paper.pdf (family 337). Any checker written for this issue must use the paren-safe pattern, and its baseline is 0 broken links, not 1.

title: Test proof density as a ledger signal before adding it as a column
description:

Follow the conditional-tag discipline: a new signal is only quotable after it discriminates. If proof density separates nothing, record the null result in notes/ and do not add the column; if it does, add it via the generated-index-column-change procedure, which keeps broad rules out of first-match chains and proves additivity by diffing the ledger column by column.

Why it matters: if the overview.tex abstract is a summary rather than the manuscript abstract, the shapes tags are keyed to a paraphrase, and the conditional-tag lesson (9 flagged, 5 real) says a tag built on thin text overstates. Record findings in notes/abstracts.md, one entry per divergent family, stating which text the tag should read.

title: Add an on-demand SQLite FTS layer over the manuscript corpus
description:
Only if the TSV index proves too blunt for term queries. notes/scripts/build_index_db.py builds a SQLite database with an FTS5 table over the 7,729 .tex files (128 MB) plus the 372 family abstracts, from the tracked TSV edge lists. The database is a generated artifact: gitignored, rebuilt by script, never committed.

This is the layer that answers "manifold" inside manuscript bodies rather than in titles, and it is the honest answer to the graph-database request: stdlib sqlite3, no server, no binary in git, and the same TSV as the source of truth. Measure query time for a 128 MB FTS build and report it before recommending the layer as routine.
